title: بهار — spring

STORY.evidence: Clear four-beat arc with one continuous world: rain (t=1.5s), a single drop hits the soil at 2.5s (contact frame), the camera dives through the surface (t=9.4s), the seed cracks at 11.2s, root and shoot grow (t=14.5s), the shoot breaks the surface and the dawn comes (t=19.4s). The hook is real but quiet - the first 2.4s are only rain, and the 'wake' beat at 11.2s is a thin crack plus a glow, weaker than the dive that precedes it.

SCRIPT.evidence: Four lines, none repeated, each 2.7-3.5s on screen: «باران که می‌آید، دانه بیدار می‌شود» (3.0-6.6s), «ریشه راهش را پیدا می‌کند» (9.6-12.6s), «ساقه به سمت نور می‌رود» (13.2-15.9s), «بهار / از زیر خاک شروع می‌شود» (17.6s). The close adds information instead of restating (C1-07 fixed). Line 3 is the weakest: it describes the picture instead of adding to it.

VISUAL.evidence: Four depth layers (sky gradient, two ridges, soil cross-section, rain front) with grain and vignette present (t=6s frame). The dawn halo at the horizon and the rim-lit seed (t=14.5s) are the best moments. Deductions: the soil is a flat brown plane whose only texture is scattered pebbles that read as beans, the shoot is a single unshaded green stroke, and the sky above ground is almost empty for the first 6s.

MOTION.evidence: Four named easings with distinct jobs (settle/outBack on the camera arrival at 9.8s, reveal/outExpo on root and shoot growth, enter/outCubic on copy, ambient on the dawn). Leaves and copy stagger; the world is continuous, so there is not a single cut to judder. Deduction: the dive is the only move with real energy - root growth and the shoot's rise read as steady progress rather than a performance, and the leaves pop (outBack) instead of unfurling.

TYPO.evidence: Body 100px (5.2% of height), hero 210px (10.9%), sub 88px: hierarchy is now readable at thumbnail size and every line fits the safe width (t=6s and t=14.5s frames). One line at a time, verified numerically with film.copyAlpha(9/17/19) = all 0 outside their windows (C1-02 fixed). Deduction: the hero is 210px against the 230px token, so the payoff is slightly under-weighted.

AUDIO.evidence: 17 cues, -14.0 LUFS integrated, true peak -1.3 dBTP, last 0.25s -72.74 dBFS, max 3 simultaneous audible (output/clip-02/verify.json). The mix is clean and cues are audible, but the bed (corporate/clean, 120 BPM) does not match the film's weather - it reads as a product video under a rain scene, and the true peak is only 0.3 dB from the ceiling.

SYNC.evidence: Cue deltas are 0.0 ms on every contact (verify.json); copy enters at 3.0 / 9.6 / 13.2 / 17.6s and the hero lands with the dawn lift at 17.6s; the drop's thud sits exactly on the splash ring at 2.5s (t=3.2s frame). Deduction: the bed's own accents do not line up with the picture beats, so the film feels driven by the edit rather than by the music.

TECH.evidence: 1080x1920 @30fps, yuv420p, 600 frames, keyframe every 60 frames (2.0s), qc-check found 0 black and 0 freeze frames, -14.0 LUFS. Deductions: 11.4 Mbps (28 MB for 20s) is heavy for a social cut - the grain at crf 16 is expensive - and the render itself ran at 1.3 fps (7m43s) because the grain was re-filled per frame.

OVERALL.evidence: In order (t=1.5, 3.2, 6, 9.4, 12, 14.5, 16.5, 19.4) it is a coherent, watchable piece with a real idea (the camera earns the cross-section) and one clear payoff. It still reads as a well-made explainer rather than a designed film: flat soil, one-note lighting, and a bed that belongs to another genre.

issues.description: Type tokens: body is now 100px (5.2%) and the hero 210px (10.9%) - hierarchy fixed, hero still 20px under the 12% token.
issues.root_cause: The token is enforced by eye in the film, not by a check; PF.drawLine can shrink a line but nothing asserts a minimum hero size.
issues.skill_change: PF.drawLine gains a `minPx` guard in v3.2; the checklist asks for the hero's measured px in the clip record.

issues.description: Overlapping copy lines: gone. copyAlpha(9/17/19) returns 0 for every line outside its window; t=6s and t=14.5s each show exactly one line.
Hard-edged light polygon: gone. The dawn is built from a radial glow plus three PF.beam sprites with soft cross-fades (t=19.4s).
No texture: fixed - grain and vignette are applied every frame; the soil now has speckles, strata and a topsoil band.
Contact beats: fixed. The drop visibly hits the soil line with rings and splash at 2.5s, and the shoot breaks the surface between 16.2 and 18.6s (t=19.4s frame).
issues.root_cause: Fixed via PF.win plus an explicit contact frame in the storyboard.

issues.description: One easing for everything: fixed - settle/reveal/enter/ambient all appear with distinct jobs.
issues.root_cause: Fixed at the source (PF.motion + per-segment easing in kf).

issues.description: Redundant closing line: fixed - «از زیر خاک شروع می‌شود» adds the consequence the three previous lines did not state.
Unsupported event type (ambient): not exercised in this clip; the events file only uses supported types.
The soil cross-section reads as a flat brown plane: its only texture is ~34 pebbles that look like scattered beans, and the strata seams are too faint to give scale.
issues.root_cause: references/palettes.md says 'texture at low opacity' but gives no recipe for a material surface; procedural speckle + ellipse pebbles is the cheapest thing that passes a still, and it fails at 100% playback.
issues.skill_change: v3.2 palettes.md gains a 'material recipes' block (soil/water/stone: layered gradients + 3 scale bands + edge occlusion); pebbles must sit in shadow pockets, not float on top.

issues.description: Delivery is 11.4 Mbps (28 MB / 20 s) and the render ran at 1.3 fps (7m43s for 600 frames).
issues.root_cause: PF.grain filled the whole canvas with an overlay pattern every frame - the single most expensive call in the film - and the encoder was asked to preserve that noise at crf 16.
issues.skill_change: Grain is now three pre-baked full-frame layers blitted with drawImage; capture.mjs exposes --crf (default 18) and reports the measured bitrate in the render summary.

issues.description: Music mood mismatch: a corporate/clean bed under a rain-and-growth film; the picture is slower and softer than the track's drive.
issues.root_cause: The track was chosen for its tempo match (120 BPM) because the kit's warm/emotional tracks are 110 BPM and the film was cut at 120; tempo was allowed to outrank mood.
issues.skill_change: v3.2 audio.md: choose the track first, then cut the film at that track's BPM (the film's tempo is a consequence of the music, not the other way round).

issues.description: True peak -1.3 dBTP is 0.3 dB from the -1.0 ceiling - legal but with no headroom.
issues.root_cause: build_sound targets -14 LUFS with a TP -1.5 limiter, but the summed cues push the peak up afterwards.
issues.skill_change: v3.2 audio.md: after the mix, re-check TP and lower the master 0.5 dB if it lands above -1.6.

issues.description: Leaves pop into place with outBack instead of unfurling; the two leaves at the tip stay small until the last second.
issues.root_cause: The leaf draw has no growth curve of its own - scale comes from the reveal progress only.
issues.skill_change: v3.2 motion.md: organic growth needs two curves (length then width) with a 0.15s offset.

notes: First clip built on the v3.1 craft kit. Every critical issue from clip 1 is closed; the remaining defects are material/lighting craft and music choice, which is exactly what clip 3 targets.
